question: In the Li3PO4-coated NCM study, how much did the charge-transfer resistance rise over 50 cycles for the bare and the coated material, and what capacity did each retain after 100 cycles at 1C?
expect: bare 27.99 to 224.04 Ω, coated 14.88 to 144.75 Ω (p8.L38-40); retention 75.4% bare vs 88.4% coated (p8.L34-36)
rendered:
According to the text in the document, for the bare NCM material, the charge-transfer resistance (Rct) increased from 27.99 to 224.04 Ω during 50 cycles, whereas for the LPO-coated NCM material, it only increased from 14.88 to 144.75 Ω.

After 100 cycles at 1C, the bare NCM retained 75.4% of its initial discharge capacity, while the LPO-coated NCM showed slow capacity fade with a capacity retention of 88.4%.
